title: Affine conversion to three-literal clauses
statement: Let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$, let $\lambda:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, and suppose a family of finite-seed OXR testers, one for each positive dimension, has a finite allowed set of predicates; satisfies $0<\alpha<\beta\le1$; and has an error function $\lambda$ taking $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$ and tending to zero as its positive argument tends to zero. Suppose every test uses an allowed predicate, every coordinate dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, and every function whose stable influences at correlation $1-\varepsilon$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha+\lambda(\varepsilon)$ for each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$. The associated testers obtained by replacing each OXR test with a randomized three-literal clause test have a finite allowed predicate set, completeness threshold $\frac12+\frac\beta2$, soundness threshold $\frac12+\frac\alpha2$, and error function $\varepsilon\mapsto\lambda(\varepsilon)/2$, with the same predicate-use, dictator-completeness, and low-influence soundness properties.
hypotheses_covered: A family of OXR testers is given for every positive dimension
The original allowed predicate set is finite
The error function tends to zero as its positive input tends to zero
Every original test uses an allowed OXR predicate
Every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$
Every function with all stable influences at correlation $1-\varepsilon$ at most $\varepsilon$ has acceptance probability at most $\alpha+\lambda(\varepsilon)$ for $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$
